recipes.name: Curried Pasta
recipes.description: A one-pot wonder — lentils, pasta and a proper curry base all cooked together under pressure. Comfort food from a small kitchen.

stages.name: Ingredient gathering
steps: Tinned tomatoes (1 can)
Red lentils (handful)
Pasta (2 large handfuls)
Onion (1 medium)
Ginger-garlic paste (1 tbsp)
Cumin seeds (1 tsp)
Ground coriander (1 tsp)
Garam masala (½ tsp)
Turmeric (½ tsp)
Chilli flakes (to taste)
Oil (2 tbsp)
Water (~2.5 cups)

stages.name: Choppy bit
steps: Dice the onion fairly fine — it'll cook down under pressure so no need to be precious
If using fresh ginger and garlic, mince or grate them now (or just use paste, no shame)

stages.name: Fry-y bit
steps: Set Foodi to sauté, heat the oil
Add cumin seeds — wait for them to pop and go fragrant (30 seconds ish)
Add onion, cook until softened and going golden (5–7 min)
Add ginger-garlic paste, stir for a minute
Add turmeric, ground coriander, chilli flakes — stir and let it fry for 30 seconds
Pour in the tinned tomatoes and stir everything together
Let the tomato base bubble for 2–3 minutes to cook out the raw taste

stages.name: Pressure cook
steps: Add red lentils and pasta directly into the pot
Pour in ~2.5 cups of water — enough to just cover everything
Give it a good stir, make sure nothing is stuck to the bottom
Seal the lid, set to pressure cook HIGH for 5 minutes
Natural release for 5 minutes, then quick release the rest

stages.name: Post pressure cook
steps: Stir well — it'll look thick and glossy
Add garam masala now and stir through
Taste and adjust salt and chilli
Wilt in a handful of spinach if you have it
Finish with a squeeze of lime and fresh coriander

notes: The pasta absorbs a lot — if it's too thick just add a splash of hot water and stir
Red lentils dissolve almost completely and thicken the sauce beautifully
Works great with chickpeas instead of lentils for a chunkier texture

recipes.name: Chana Dal
recipes.description: Split yellow peas cooked low and slow under pressure into a thick, deeply spiced dal. Dead simple, deeply satisfying.

stages.name: Ingredient gathering
steps: Chana dal / split yellow peas (200g) — soaked 30 min if you have time
Onion (1 large)
Tinned tomatoes (1 can)
Ginger-garlic paste (1 tbsp)
Cumin seeds (1 tsp)
Mustard seeds (½ tsp)
Turmeric (½ tsp)
Ground cumin (1 tsp)
Ground coriander (1 tsp)
Garam masala (½ tsp)
Dried chilli or chilli flakes (to taste)
Oil (2 tbsp)
Water (3 cups)

stages.name: Choppy bit
steps: Dice the onion
Rinse the chana dal well until the water runs clear

stages.name: Fry-y bit
steps: Sauté mode, heat oil until shimmering
Add mustard seeds — wait for them to pop, then add cumin seeds
Add onion, cook down until deep golden — take your time here, 8–10 min
Add ginger-garlic paste, fry 1–2 minutes
Add turmeric, ground cumin, ground coriander and chilli — fry 30 seconds
Add tomatoes, cook down for 4–5 minutes until oil starts to separate from the masala

stages.name: Pressure cook
steps: Add drained chana dal to the pot
Pour in 3 cups of water
Stir well, seal the lid
Pressure cook HIGH for 15 minutes
Natural release for 10 minutes, then quick release

stages.name: Post pressure cook
steps: Stir — the dal should be soft and some of it breaking down into the sauce
If too watery, sauté for a few minutes with the lid off to thicken
Add garam masala and stir through
Taste for salt and heat
Finish with a knob of butter or a drizzle of oil, fresh coriander, squeeze of lemon

notes: Soaking the dal cuts the pressure cook time down — skip it if you're in a hurry, just add 5 more minutes
Lovely with rice or just eaten as a thick soup straight from the bowl
The tarka (tempering the spices in oil at the start) is the most important bit — don't rush it

recipes.name: Saag Paneer Pasta
recipes.description: A caravan mashup — the rich spiced spinach base of saag paneer but with pasta cooked right in. Sounds weird, tastes brilliant.

stages.name: Ingredient gathering
steps: Paneer (200g block)
Frozen spinach (3 large cubes) or fresh (big handful)
Pasta (2 large handfuls)
Onion (1 medium)
Tinned tomatoes (½ can)
Ginger-garlic paste (1 tbsp)
Cumin seeds (1 tsp)
Turmeric (½ tsp)
Ground coriander (1 tsp)
Garam masala (½ tsp)
Kasuri methi / dried fenugreek leaves (1 tsp) — optional but worth it
Oil (2 tbsp)
Water (2 cups)

stages.name: Choppy bit
steps: Cut paneer into roughly 2cm cubes
Dice the onion

stages.name: Fry-y bit
steps: Heat oil on sauté, add paneer cubes — fry until golden on a couple of sides, set aside
In the same oil, add cumin seeds
Add onion, cook until soft and lightly golden
Add ginger-garlic paste, stir 1 minute
Add turmeric and ground coriander, fry 30 seconds
Add tomatoes, cook for 3 minutes
Add spinach (from frozen is fine), stir until wilted into the base

stages.name: Pressure cook
steps: Add pasta to the pot and stir through the spinach masala
Pour in 2 cups water — the spinach adds liquid so go a touch less than usual
Nestle the paneer pieces back in on top
Seal lid, pressure cook HIGH 4 minutes
Quick release

stages.name: Post pressure cook
steps: Stir gently — the paneer will be soft so don't mash it
Add garam masala and kasuri methi, stir through
The sauce should be thick and clinging to the pasta
Taste for salt
Finish with a little cream or yoghurt swirled through if you have it

notes: Frozen spinach works great here — no need to defrost first
Kasuri methi gives it that proper restaurant saag flavour — find it in any Asian supermarket
If the sauce is too thick after pressure cooking, a splash of hot water loosens it right up

recipes.name: Aloo Chana
recipes.description: Potatoes and chickpeas in a thick, tangy tomato masala. A proper filling caravan meal that costs almost nothing.

stages.name: Ingredient gathering
steps: Potatoes (2 medium)
Tinned chickpeas (1 can, drained)
Tinned tomatoes (1 can)
Onion (1 medium)
Ginger-garlic paste (1 tbsp)
Cumin seeds (1 tsp)
Turmeric (½ tsp)
Ground cumin (1 tsp)
Ground coriander (1 tsp)
Amchur / dried mango powder (½ tsp) — gives it the tang
Garam masala (½ tsp)
Chilli (to taste)
Oil (2 tbsp)
Water (¾ cup)

stages.name: Choppy bit
steps: Peel and chop potatoes into roughly 3cm chunks — keep them chunky so they don't dissolve
Dice the onion

stages.name: Fry-y bit
steps: Sauté mode, heat oil
Add cumin seeds, let them sizzle
Add onion, cook until golden — about 7 minutes
Add ginger-garlic paste, fry 1 minute
Add turmeric, ground cumin, ground coriander, chilli — fry 30 seconds
Add tomatoes, cook down for 4 minutes until the masala is thick

stages.name: Pressure cook
steps: Add potato chunks and drained chickpeas, stir to coat in the masala
Add ¾ cup water — not too much, you want a thick gravy not a soup
Seal lid, pressure cook HIGH 8 minutes
Natural release 5 minutes, then quick release

stages.name: Post pressure cook
steps: Stir gently — potatoes should be perfectly tender but still holding shape
Add garam masala and amchur, stir through
Mash one or two potato pieces slightly to thicken the gravy if needed
Taste for salt and tang — add more amchur if it needs a lift
Top with fresh coriander and a squeeze of lemon

notes: Amchur is the secret weapon here — it gives that classic chole tang without tamarind
Great stuffed into a wrap with some yoghurt and chutney
Waxy potatoes hold their shape better than floury ones under pressure
